page: Amazon Web Services m7i.large is a general-purpose instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8488C processor with an x86_64 architecture, providing 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core with hyper-threading. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 3.2 GHz and includes a 105 MB L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 8.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 5 GHz, yielding a 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. It does not include local storage or a GPU, and it offers a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks reveal a contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core performance is moderate, with stress-ng single-core CPU and Geekbench single-core scores falling in the average category. However, multi-core and memory-bound benchmarks show limitations. The stress-ng multi-core performance and Passmark memory scores are categorized as poor, and uncached memory read bandwidth is limited to 13.5 GB/sec. The processor supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), which assist in specialized workloads like cryptography and basic vector operations, though overall resource density restricts heavy parallel execution.

Given its hardware profile, the m7i.large is positioned as a cost-efficient option for entry-level general-purpose workloads that do not require high multi-core throughput or local storage. It is suitable for basic web serving, text processing, and lightweight application hosting. It is less suited for memory-intensive databases, software compilation, or complex multi-threaded tasks due to its lower multi-core and memory bandwidth benchmark ratings.
description: Amazon Web Services m7i.large is a general-purpose instance featuring 2 dedicated vCPUs and 1 physical core powered by an Intel Xeon 8488C processor at 3.2 GHz. Built on the Nitro hypervisor, it includes 8.0 GB of DDR5 memory at 5 GHz, but lacks local storage and GPU accelerators. The instance supports advanced CPU instructions like AVX-512 and Intel AMX. Benchmark data shows average single-core CPU and text processing performance, while multi-core execution, memory bandwidth, and database operations fall into the weak to poor categories. With a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps, this instance is best suited for lightweight general-purpose workloads, basic web serving, and single-threaded applications that do not demand high memory throughput or parallel processing power.
